about.title: San Marino Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Marino is a small, quiet city, but its households use the same appliances, vehicles, tools, and consumer goods found anywhere else in Los Angeles County — and defects don't discriminate by zip code. A malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a car part that fails on Huntington Drive, or a children's product with a hidden hazard can cause serious harm in an instant. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person usually doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused the injury. That can include design flaws, manufacturing errors, or inadequate warnings. Multiple parties along the supply chain — makers, distributors, and retailers — may share responsibility. If you were hurt by a product in San Marino, we can review what happened and help you understand your options.

whyChoose.title: Why San Marino Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, we may be able to build your case around the defect itself rather than needing to prove the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, and we can help identify who was involved in getting the product to you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact and unaltered can be important evidence, and we can advise you on how to protect it before it's lost, repaired, or thrown away.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not on the manufacturer's conduct. We can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: I still have the product that injured me — what should I do with it?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without repairing, discarding, or altering it. This preserved evidence can be important to us evaluating a defect claim. Store it somewhere safe until you've spoken with us for advice.

items.question: Does it matter that San Marino is a small city for this type of claim?
items.answer: Not really — defective product claims usually center on the product and manufacturer, not the city where the injury happened. Whether it occurred at home, near Los Robles Avenue, or elsewhere in San Marino, the same California liability principles typically apply. We can walk you through what matters in your specific case.

items.question: How do you work with injured people?
items.answer: We handle product liability claims for injured people and offer a free review of your situation. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
